```js
function buildReplyCoverage(inputThreads, replies) {
    var open = (inputThreads || []).filter(function(t) {
        return t && t.resolved !== true && !t.bot;
    });
    var targeted = {};
    (replies || []).forEach(function(r) {
        if (r && r.threadId) targeted[String(r.threadId)] = true;
    });
    var covered = [];
    var unaddressed = [];
    open.forEach(function(t) {
        var id = t.threadId ? String(t.threadId) : null;
        if (id && targeted[id]) covered.push(t);
        else unaddressed.push(t);
    });
    return {
        openThreads: open.length,
        targetedCount: covered.length,  // hmm
        unaddressed: unaddressed
    };
}
```

Wait — "fewer than N thread-targeted replies out" where N = number of unresolved threads input. Note bot threads and resolved threads shouldn't count. Hmm, AC2 says "when the input held N ≥ 1 unresolved threads, a review_replies.json with fewer than N thread-targeted replies triggers the coverage warning (log + completion comment lists the unaddressed threads by ID/title)". The input threads snapshot may include resolved/bot ones — the agent is only expected to reply to unresolved, non-bot threads (the pr_discussions.md only shows unresolved non-bot threads). So counting open non-bot threads is right.

The per-thread coverage list in log: for each unaddressed thread, log `⚠️ Thread <threadId|rootCommentId> (<path>) NOT addressed by any review_replies.json row: "<body excerpt>"`.

Completion comment: needs the list of unaddressed threads. So `buildCompletionComment` (new function) should take coverage info.

### 3. Completion honesty (live re-check) — AC3, AC4, AC5
- Before writing the completion ticket comment, post-action re-fetches PR's unresolved threads live (same call as input prep: scm.fetchDiscussions).
- Any thread that (a) appeared mid-run, or (b) was never targeted by a reply, is listed in completion comment.
- "no code changes are required" wording allowed ONLY when live unresolved-thread count is 0 AND verdict is not CHANGES_REQUESTED.
- Otherwise: "rework pushed; N review threads remain open — the SM will re-arm a threads-rework."

Current postJiraComment:
```js
function postJiraComment(tracker, ticketKey, prUrl, branchName, prCommentPosted, codeChangesCommitted, fixSummary) {
    ...
    if (codeChangesCommitted) { "✅ Rework Completed" ... "AI Teammate has addressed all PR review comments and pushed the fixes." }
    else { "✅ Rework Analysis Completed" ... "AI Teammate analyzed all PR review comments and determined no code changes are required." }
```

New design: refactor into a pure `buildReworkCompletionComment(flavor-ish, ctx)` for testability, where ctx includes: codeChangesCommitted, prUrl, branchName, prCommentPosted, liveOpenThreads (array), verdict (CHANGES_REQUESTED/APPROVED/null), unaddressed (array from coverage).

Wording rules (gh-799):
- "no code changes are required" ONLY when live unresolved-thread count is 0 AND verdict !== CHANGES_REQUESTED.
- Everything else (live count > 0): truthful form "rework pushed; N review threads remain open — the SM will re-arm a threads-rework." plus list unaddressed/drift threads by ID/title.

Wait — but should the truthful form replace "Rework Completed" when codeChangesCommitted? The ticket says: "the 'no code changes are required' wording is allowed ONLY when the live unresolved-thread count is 0 AND the verdict is not CHANGES_REQUESTED. Everything else gets the truthful form: 'rework pushed; N review threads remain open — the SM will re-arm a threads-rework.'"

The "no code changes are required" wording appears in the `codeChangesCommitted=false` branch. So:
- If live open threads > 0 → the completion comment must include the truthful form and list open threads. Even if code changes were committed (the "has addressed all PR review comments" claim is also dishonest then). The truthful form: "rework pushed; N review threads remain open — the SM will re-arm a threads-rework."
- If live count 0 and verdict not CHANGES_REQUESTED → existing behavior preserved (AC4).

Hmm, but what about the case codeChangesCommitted=true and live threads=0 and verdict=CHANGES_REQUESTED? "Everything else gets the truthful form" — verdict is CHANGES_REQUESTED but threads are 0. The "no code changes" wording isn't in play since codeChangesCommitted=true. The wording rule targets the "no code changes required" claim specifically. But strictly: "Everything else gets the truthful form: 'rework pushed; N review threads remain open...'". Hmm — if threads are 0 but verdict is CHANGES_REQUESTED, saying "N review threads remain open" with N=0 makes no sense. Let me interpret: the "no code changes are required" wording is allowed only when (live 0 AND verdict != CHANGES_REQUESTED). "Everything else" = when live threads > 0, get the threads-remain-open form. For live 0 + CHANGES_REQUESTED verdict — an odd corner. I think a sensible mapping:

- live open threads > 0 → truthful form with the open thread list (regardless of codeChangesCommitted), title maybe still "✅ Rework Completed" or "⚠️"? The incident shape: completion claimed while threads open. For honesty, the comment must say N threads remain open. Title: keep "✅ Rework Completed"? Hmm. The ticket: "the completion comment lists the unaddressed threads" and "rework pushed; N review threads remain open — the SM will re-arm a threads-rework." I'd title it "🔧 Rework Completed with Open Threads" or keep "✅ Rework Completed" plus the honest body. Let me keep it simple and truthful:
  - Header: `⚠️ Rework Completed — N review thread(s) remain open` (when open > 0)
  - Body: "rework pushed; N review threads remain open — the SM will re-arm a threads-rework." + per-thread list (ID, path, title/excerpt) marking unaddressed vs mid-run-appearing.
- codeChangesCommitted=true, live 0, verdict CHANGES_REQUESTED → keep "✅ Rework Completed ... addressed all ... pushed fixes"? That claims "addressed all PR review comments" while verdict is CHANGES_REQUESTED. Hmm — with 0 unresolved threads and CHANGES_REQUESTED verdict, someone left a review-level verdict but no open threads. The existing wording would stay (per AC4-ish preservation for clean path). But the "no code changes required" is only the codeChangesCommitted=false branch. For safety per the contract: "the 'no code changes are required' wording is allowed ONLY when the live unresolved-thread count is 0 AND the verdict is not CHANGES_REQUESTED" — so in the codeChangesCommitted=false branch with live 0 + CHANGES_REQUESTED, we can't say "no code changes required"; use a neutral wording instead: "Rework analysis completed — no code changes were required by the open review threads, but the latest review verdict is CHANGES_REQUESTED; the SM will re-check." Hmm, that's inventing. Let me re-read AC3: "the completion comment is generated from a LIVE unresolved-threads fetch; a run with 2 open threads never produces the 'no code changes are required' wording (unit-tested wording selection)."

So the unit-tested wording selection: given {input threads × live threads × verdict}, select wording:
- live > 0 → threads-remain-open form (lists them). Never "no code changes are required".
- live == 0 && verdict != CHANGES_REQUESTED → existing wording/behavior (AC4).
- live == 0 && verdict == CHANGES_REQUESTED → hmm. "Everything else gets the truthful form" — I'll use a form that says the rework pushed and the review verdict still requires changes: e.g. "rework pushed; the latest review verdict remains CHANGES_REQUESTED (0 unresolved threads) — the SM will re-check." Actually, wait. Let me think about what actually happens in the machine loop: with 0 unresolved threads and CHANGES_REQUESTED, the re-review armer runs on verdict... The truthful thing is to not claim "no code changes are required" and instead state the verdict. I'll implement:

```js
function selectReworkCompletionWording(liveOpenThreads, verdict) {
    // returns 'clean' | 'open-threads' | 'verdict-changes-requested'
    if (liveOpenThreads > 0) return 'open-threads';
    if (verdict === 'CHANGES_REQUESTED') return 'verdict-changes-requested';
    return 'clean';
}
```

And the builder uses it. The 'clean' + codeChangesCommitted=false → existing "no code changes are required" wording. The verdict-changes-requested case → honest statement that verdict remains CHANGES_REQUESTED.

Now — the postJiraComment signature. It's exported? No — module.exports doesn't include postJiraComment. It's internal to action(). I can refactor it into:
- `buildReworkCompletionComment(m, ctx)` — pure, exported for tests. m = commentMarkup flavor; ctx = { ticketKey, prUrl, branchName, prCommentPosted, codeChangesCommitted, liveOpenThreads, verdict, unaddressedThreads, driftThreads }.
- Keep `postJiraComment` as the poster that first fetches live state and then calls the builder. Actually postJiraComment currently takes fixed args. I'll rework postJiraComment to accept a live-state provider or fetch in action().

```js
function fetchLiveUnresolvedThreads(scm, pr) {

}
```

Fail-open in the honest direction: if the live fetch fails, we can't prove 0 open threads → treat as unknown; the honest choice: keep "no code changes" only if input had 0 threads and verdict != CHANGES_REQUESTED... Hmm. But the live fetch is the gate. If the fetch fails, we should warn but not block the completion. Per repo convention (headMovedSinceLastReview fail-open), a broken probe must not stall the loop. For honesty: on probe failure, fall back to the input snapshot threads (the best known data) — i.e. `liveOpenThreads = inputUnresolvedCount` when the probe fails. That means: probe fails + input had threads → truthful form. Probe fails + input 0 threads → clean path preserved (can't do better). That's conservative-honest and never stalls. Good.

With my design: liveOpenThreads=2, input 0 → open-threads form; the comment lists the live threads, and I can mark which were input vs new (drift). Coverage: unaddressed = input threads not targeted by replies; drift = live threads whose threadId not input snapshot (appeared mid-run). The completion comment lists all live open threads: `(unaddressed ∪ drift)` — actually all live open threads, each labeled: "not addressed by any reply" or "new since rework started" or "targeted but still open".

Let me define the completion comment builder inputs:
- `liveOpenThreads`: array of threads (with threadId, path, body excerpt)
- `inputThreadIds`: set of threadIds from input snapshot
- `unaddressedIds`: set of input open threads not targeted by replies

Per-thread label:
- if threadId not inputThreadIds → "🆕 appeared mid-run"
- else if in unaddressedIds → "not addressed by any review reply"
- else → "reply posted, thread still open" (reply targeted it but live it's still unresolved — resolution failed or reviewer reopened)

Nice — thread-by-thread accounting per ticket.

Now the LOUD warning for coverage (AC2) also needs the log + completion comment. The completion comment for open threads lists unaddressed threads by ID/title. ✓.

In action, before postThreadReplies, read input threads + replies (to compute coverage) — but postThreadReplies parses review_replies.json itself. To avoid double-parsing, postThreadReplies can compute and RETURN coverage... but changing its return from number to object breaks existing tests (`assert.equal(posted, 1)`). REG requirement says "existing rework post-action tests stay green on the clean path (AC4)". Changing return type means updating the test file's assertions — that's modifying existing tests. # gh-799: [ENH] Rework context preparation: guaranteed-complete rework picture (threads+CI+verdict) and honest live-rechecked completion — live: fa PR #1420

## Description

## Goal — Rework context preparation: guaranteed-complete rework picture + honest completion contract (v1)

One sentence: **every rework leg starts with the COMPLETE open-item picture of its PR (threads with IDs, CI failures, review verdict — regardless of which armer fired) and ends with a completion step that re-checks the PR live and never declares "no code changes required" while unresolved threads exist.**

Live evidence (fa PR #1420 / gh-1415, 2026-10-08): the CI-red-armed rework leg (run 37806292238) finished with `outputs/review_replies.json` carrying `"threadId": null` (untargeted reply → combined PR comment), and the post-action posted **"Rework Analysis Completed — AI Teammate analyzed all PR review comments and determined no code changes are required"** — while the PR's review state required changes. The threads themselves arrived later (18:56, posted by the follow-up review), so the input was honest at leg start — but the completion claim was written from the STALE input snapshot, not from the live PR, and nothing in the contract forces the agent to bind replies to thread IDs when threads exist. The machine loop self-corrected (threads-armer → second rework leg → 4/4 threads resolved), at the cost of an extra full leg + tokens and a misleading completion comment on the ticket.

## Why this framing

- `preCliReworkSetup.js` already fetches both halves of the picture (`ci_failures.md` step 4.7 + `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` → `pr_discussions.md` / `pr_discussions_raw.json` with IDs, step 5) — this card does not rebuild the pipeline; it closes three CONTRACT gaps around it: reply targeting, mid-run drift, and completion honesty.
- The silent-update race that also surfaced in the same leg is a separate card (#798) — out of scope here.

## Architecture

Three contract hardenings, all inside the existing rework pipeline (`preCliReworkSetup.js` input prep → `run-agent.sh` leg → `pushReworkChanges.js` post-action):

1. **Input completeness is armer-independent (pin it).** Whatever arms the leg (fail-validation CI-red, review-threads-resolved armer, conflict-rework, manual dispatch), the input folder must always carry: `pr_discussions_raw.json` (unresolved threads with IDs), `ci_failures.md` (failed checks), and a new `review_state.md` — the review verdict(s) + decision state (`CHANGES_REQUESTED` / `APPROVED` / none) — so the agent sees WHAT the reviewer asked, not just raw threads. # Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent

# gh-799: [ENH] Rework context preparation: guaranteed-complete rework picture (threads+CI+verdict) and honest live-rechecked completion — live: fa PR #1420

## Description

## Goal — Rework context preparation: guaranteed-complete rework picture + honest completion contract (v1)

One sentence: **every rework leg starts with the COMPLETE open-item picture of its PR (threads with IDs, CI failures, review verdict — regardless of which armer fired) and ends with a completion step that re-checks the PR live and never declares "no code changes required" while unresolved threads exist.**

Live evidence (fa PR #1420 / gh-1415, 2026-10-08): the CI-red-armed rework leg (run 37806292238) finished with `outputs/review_replies.json` carrying `"threadId": null` (untargeted reply → combined PR comment), and the post-action posted **"Rework Analysis Completed — AI Teammate analyzed all PR review comments and determined no code changes are required"** — while the PR's review state required changes. The threads themselves arrived later (18:56, posted by the follow-up review), so the input was honest at leg start — but the completion claim was written from the STALE input snapshot, not from the live PR, and nothing in the contract forces the agent to bind replies to thread IDs when threads exist. The machine loop self-corrected (threads-armer → second rework leg → 4/4 threads resolved), at the cost of an extra full leg + tokens and a misleading completion comment on the ticket.

## Why this framing

- `preCliReworkSetup.js` already fetches both halves of the picture (`ci_failures.md` step 4.7 + `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` → `pr_discussions.md` / `pr_discussions_raw.json` with IDs, step 5) — this card does not rebuild the pipeline; it closes three CONTRACT gaps around it: reply targeting, mid-run drift, and completion honesty.
- The silent-update race that also surfaced in the same leg is a separate card (#798) — out of scope here.

## Architecture

Three contract hardenings, all inside the existing rework pipeline (`preCliReworkSetup.js` input prep → `run-agent.sh` leg → `pushReworkChanges.js` post-action):

1. **Input completeness is armer-independent (pin it).** Whatever arms the leg (fail-validation CI-red, review-threads-resolved armer, conflict-rework, manual dispatch), the input folder must always carry: `pr_discussions_raw.json` (unresolved threads with IDs), `ci_failures.md` (failed checks), and a new `review_state.md` — the review verdict(s) + decision state (`CHANGES_REQUESTED` / `APPROVED` / none) — so the agent sees WHAT the reviewer asked, not just raw threads. Today the first two happen to be fetched; this card makes the trio a pinned contract with a test each (an armer that skips one is a regression).
2. **Reply-targeting contract.** `review_replies.json` rows must carry a non-null `threadId` whenever `pr_discussions_raw.json` held ≥1 unresolved thread at leg start; the post-action must treat "N threads in, fewer than N targeted replies out" as a LOUD warning state (per-thread coverage list in the log + completion comment), never silently fold untargeted replies into a "nothing required" story.
3. **Completion honesty (live re-check).** Before writing the completion ticket comment, the post-action re-fetches the PR's unresolved threads live (same call as input prep). Any thread that (a) appeared mid-run, or (b) was never targeted by a reply, is listed in the completion comment; the "no code changes are required" wording is allowed ONLY when the live unresolved-thread count is 0 AND the verdict is not CHANGES_REQUESTED. Everything else gets the truthful form: "rework pushed; N review threads remain open — the SM will re-arm a threads-rework."

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent

# gh-799: [ENH] Rework context preparation: guaranteed-complete rework picture (threads+CI+verdict) and honest live-rechecked completion — live: fa PR #1420

## Description

## Goal — Rework context preparation: guaranteed-complete rework picture + honest completion contract (v1)

One sentence: **every rework leg starts with the COMPLETE open-item picture of its PR (threads with IDs, CI failures, review verdict — regardless of which armer fired) and ends with a completion step that re-checks the PR live and never declares "no code changes required" while unresolved threads exist.**

Live evidence (fa PR #1420 / gh-1415, 2026-10-08): the CI-red-armed rework leg (run 37806292238) finished with `outputs/review_replies.json` carrying `"threadId": null` (untargeted reply → combined PR comment), and the post-action posted **"Rework Analysis Completed — AI Teammate analyzed all PR review comments and determined no code changes are required"** — while the PR's review state required changes. The threads themselves arrived later (18:56, posted by the follow-up review), so the input was honest at leg start — but the completion claim was written from the STALE input snapshot, not from the live PR, and nothing in the contract forces the agent to bind replies to thread IDs when threads exist. The machine loop self-corrected (threads-armer → second rework leg → 4/4 threads resolved), at the cost of an extra full leg + tokens and a misleading completion comment on the ticket.

## Why this framing

- `preCliReworkSetup.js` already fetches both halves of the picture (`ci_failures.md` step 4.7 + `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` → `pr_discussions.md` / `pr_discussions_raw.json` with IDs, step 5) — this card does not rebuild the pipeline; it closes three CONTRACT gaps around it: reply targeting, mid-run drift, and completion honesty.
- The silent-update race that also surfaced in the same leg is a separate card (#798) — out of scope here.

## Architecture

Three contract hardenings, all inside the existing rework pipeline (`preCliReworkSetup.js` input prep → `run-agent.sh` leg → `pushReworkChanges.js` post-action):

1. **Input completeness is armer-independent (pin it).** Whatever arms the leg (fail-validation CI-red, review-threads-resolved armer, conflict-rework, manual dispatch), the input folder must always carry: `pr_discussions_raw.json` (unresolved threads with IDs), `ci_failures.md` (failed checks), and a new `review_state.md` — the review verdict(s) + decision state (`CHANGES_REQUESTED` / `APPROVED` / none) — so the agent sees WHAT the reviewer asked, not just raw threads. Today the first two happen to be fetched; this card makes the trio a pinned contract with a test each (an armer that skips one is a regression).
2. **Reply-targeting contract.** `review_replies.json` rows must carry a non-null `threadId` whenever `pr_discussions_raw.json` held ≥1 unresolved thread at leg start; the post-action must treat "N threads in, fewer than N targeted replies out" as a LOUD warning state (per-thread coverage list in the log + completion comment), never silently fold untargeted replies into a "nothing required" story.
3. **Completion honesty (live re-check).** Before writing the completion ticket comment, the post-action re-fetches the PR's unresolved threads live (same call as input prep). Any thread that (a) appeared mid-run, or (b) was never targeted by a reply, is listed in the completion comment; the "no code changes are required" wording is allowed ONLY when the live unresolved-thread count is 0 AND the verdict is not CHANGES_REQUESTED. # Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent

One sentence: **every rework leg starts with the COMPLETE open-item picture of its PR (threads with IDs, CI failures, review verdict — regardless of which armer fired) and ends with a completion step that re-checks the PR live and never declares "no code changes required" while unresolved threads exist.**

Live evidence (fa PR #1420 / gh-1415, 2026-10-08): the CI-red-armed rework leg (run 37806292238) finished with `outputs/review_replies.json` carrying `"threadId": null` (untargeted reply → combined PR comment), and the post-action posted **"Rework Analysis Completed — AI Teammate analyzed all PR review comments and determined no code changes are required"** — while the PR's review state required changes. The threads themselves arrived later (18:56, posted by the follow-up review), so the input was honest at leg start — but the completion claim was written from the STALE input snapshot, not from the live PR, and nothing in the contract forces the agent to bind replies to thread IDs when threads exist. The machine loop self-corrected (threads-armer → second rework leg → 4/4 threads resolved), at the cost of an extra full leg + tokens and a misleading completion comment on the ticket.

## Why this framing

- `preCliReworkSetup.js` already fetches both halves of the picture (`ci_failures.md` step 4.7 + `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` → `pr_discussions.md` / `pr_discussions_raw.json` with IDs, step 5) — this card does not rebuild the pipeline; it closes three CONTRACT gaps around it: reply targeting, mid-run drift, and completion honesty.
- The silent-update race that also surfaced in the same leg is a separate card (#798) — out of scope here.

## Architecture

Three contract hardenings, all inside the existing rework pipeline (`preCliReworkSetup.js` input prep → `run-agent.sh` leg → `pushReworkChanges.js` post-action):

1. **Input completeness is armer-independent (pin it).** Whatever arms the leg (fail-validation CI-red, review-threads-resolved armer, conflict-rework, manual dispatch), the input folder must always carry: `pr_discussions_raw.json` (unresolved threads with IDs), `ci_failures.md` (failed checks), and a new `review_state.md` — the review verdict(s) + decision state (`CHANGES_REQUESTED` / `APPROVED` / none) — so the agent sees WHAT the reviewer asked, not just raw threads. Today the first two happen to be fetched; this card makes the trio a pinned contract with a test each (an armer that skips one is a regression).
2. **Reply-targeting contract.** `review_replies.json` rows must carry a non-null `threadId` whenever `pr_discussions_raw.json` held ≥1 unresolved thread at leg start; the post-action must treat "N threads in, fewer than N targeted replies out" as a LOUD warning state (per-thread coverage list in the log + completion comment), never silently fold untargeted replies into a "nothing required" story.
3. **Completion honesty (live re-check).** Before writing the completion ticket comment, the post-action re-fetches the PR's unresolved threads live (same call as input prep). Any thread that (a) appeared mid-run, or (b) was never targeted by a reply, is listed in the completion comment; the "no code changes are required" wording is allowed ONLY when the live unresolved-thread count is 0 AND the verdict is not CHANGES_REQUESTED. Everything else gets the truthful form: "rework pushed; N review threads remain open — the SM will re-arm a threads-rework."

## Capability surface

| step | today | after |
|---|---|---|
| input folder | threads + CI failures fetched (happens today, unpinned) | pinned trio + `review_state.md` verdict context, contract-tested |
| `review_replies.json` | threadId may be null even when threads exist | per-thread targeting required; coverage gap = loud warning |
| completion comment | template may claim "no code changes required" regardless of live state | live unresolved-thread re-check; honest wording, thread-by-thread accounting |
| machine loop | extra self-correction leg + misleading comment | one pass closes CI + threads; completion states exactly what remains |

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — a rework leg armed by ANY armer produces an input folder containing non-empty `pr_discussions_raw.json`, `ci_failures.md`, and `review_state.md` (fixture-tested per armer path).
- **AC2** — when the input held N ≥ 1 unresolved threads, a `review_replies.json` with fewer than N thread-targeted replies triggers the coverage warning (log + completion comment lists the unaddressed threads by ID/title).
- **AC3** — the completion comment is generated from a LIVE unresolved-threads fetch; a run with 2 open threads never produces the "no code changes are required" wording (unit-tested wording selection).
- **AC4** — with 0 unresolved threads and a non-CHANGES_REQUESTED verdict, the existing wording/behavior is preserved (no regression for the clean path).
- **AC5** — mid-run-appearing threads (input 0 threads, live ≥ 1 at completion) are reported in the completion comment (drift case, exactly the live incident shape).

## Test plan

- `UT-*` — `preCliReworkSetup` input-trio tests per armer fixture (AC1); `pushReworkChanges` wording-selection tests over {input threads × live threads × verdict} (AC2–AC5); coverage-counter test for reply targeting (AC2).
- `IT-*` — hermetic end-to-end of the rework pipeline with mocked SCM: drift fixture (threads appear mid-run) → completion lists them (AC5).
- `REG` — full `run_all.json` green; existing rework post-action tests stay green on the clean path (AC4).

## Non-goals

- Combining the CI-rework and threads-rework ARMERS into one rule (the armers stay separate; this card makes the LEG complete regardless of armer).
- #798 (silent-update vs in-flight leg race) — separate card, already filed.
- Changing the reply file format beyond requiring non-null threadId when threads exist (consumers elsewhere read this shape).

## Open questions

- Should `review_state.md` carry the reviewer's per-thread severity (BLOCKING/SUGGESTION) so the agent can prioritize? (GraphQL exposes it; recommend yes — cheap and useful.)

## References

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent

# gh-799: [ENH] Rework context preparation: guaranteed-complete rework picture (threads+CI+verdict) and honest live-rechecked completion — live: fa PR #1420

## Description

## Goal — Rework context preparation: guaranteed-complete rework picture + honest completion contract (v1)

One sentence: **every rework leg starts with the COMPLETE open-item picture of its PR (threads with IDs, CI failures, review verdict — regardless of which armer fired) and ends with a completion step that re-checks the PR live and never declares "no code changes required" while unresolved threads exist.**

Live evidence (fa PR #1420 / gh-1415, 2026-10-08): the CI-red-armed rework leg (run 37806292238) finished with `outputs/review_replies.json` carrying `"threadId": null` (untargeted reply → combined PR comment), and the post-action posted **"Rework Analysis Completed — AI Teammate analyzed all PR review comments and determined no code changes are required"** — while the PR's review state required changes. The threads themselves arrived later (18:56, posted by the follow-up review), so the input was honest at leg start — but the completion claim was written from the STALE input snapshot, not from the live PR, and nothing in the contract forces the agent to bind replies to thread IDs when threads exist. The machine loop self-corrected (threads-armer → second rework leg → 4/4 threads resolved), at the cost of an extra full leg + tokens and a misleading completion comment on the ticket.

## Why this framing

- `preCliReworkSetup.js` already fetches both halves of the picture (`ci_failures.md` step 4.7 + `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` → `pr_discussions.md` / `pr_discussions_raw.json` with IDs, step 5) — this card does not rebuild the pipeline; it closes three CONTRACT gaps around it: reply targeting, mid-run drift, and completion honesty.
- The silent-update race that also surfaced in the same leg is a separate card (#798) — out of scope here.

## Architecture

Three contract hardenings, all inside the existing rework pipeline (`preCliReworkSetup.js` input prep → `run-agent.sh` leg → `pushReworkChanges.js` post-action):

1. **Input completeness is armer-independent (pin it).** Whatever arms the leg (fail-validation CI-red, review-threads-resolved armer, conflict-rework, manual dispatch), the input folder must always carry: `pr_discussions_raw.json` (unresolved threads with IDs), `ci_failures.md` (failed checks), and a new `review_state.md` — the review verdict(s) + decision state (`CHANGES_REQUESTED` / `APPROVED` / none) — so the agent sees WHAT the reviewer asked, not just raw threads. Today the first two happen to be fetched; this card makes the trio a pinned contract with a test each (an armer that skips one is a regression).
2. **Reply-targeting contract.** `review_replies.json` rows must carry a non-null `threadId` whenever `pr_discussions_raw.json` held ≥1 unresolved thread at leg start; the post-action must treat "N threads in, fewer than N targeted replies out" as a LOUD warning state (per-thread coverage list in the log + completion comment), never silently fold untargeted replies into a "nothing required" story.
3. **Completion honesty (live re-check).** Before writing the completion ticket comment, the post-action re-fetches the PR's unresolved threads live (same call as input prep). Any thread that (a) appeared mid-run, or (b) was never targeted by a reply, is listed in the completion comment; the "no code changes are required" wording is allowed ONLY when the live unresolved-thread count is 0 AND the verdict is not CHANGES_REQUESTED. Everything else gets the truthful form: "rework pushed; N review threads remain open — the SM will re-arm a threads-rework."

## Capability surface

| step | today | after |
|---|---|---|
| input folder | threads + CI failures fetched (happens today, unpinned) | pinned trio + `review_state.md` verdict context, contract-tested |
| `review_replies.json` | threadId may be null even when threads exist | per-thread targeting required; coverage gap = loud warning |
| completion comment | template may claim "no code changes required" regardless of live state | live unresolved-thread re-check; honest wording, thread-by-thread accounting |
| machine loop | extra self-correction leg + misleading comment | one pass closes CI + threads; completion states exactly what remains |

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — a rework leg armed by ANY armer produces an input folder containing non-empty `pr_discussions_raw.json`, `ci_failures.md`, and `review_state.md` (fixture-tested per armer path).
- **AC2** — when the input held N ≥ 1 unresolved threads, a `review_replies.json` with fewer than N thread-targeted replies triggers the coverage warning (log + completion comment lists the unaddressed threads by ID/title).
- **AC3** — the completion comment is generated from a LIVE unresolved-threads fetch; a run with 2 open threads never produces the "no code changes are required" wording (unit-tested wording selection).
- **AC4** — with 0 unresolved threads and a non-CHANGES_REQUESTED verdict, the existing wording/behavior is preserved (no regression for the clean path).
- **AC5** — mid-run-appearing threads (input 0 threads, live ≥ 1 at completion) are reported in the completion comment (drift case, exactly the live incident shape).

## Test plan

- `UT-*` — `preCliReworkSetup` input-trio tests per armer fixture (AC1); `pushReworkChanges` wording-selection tests over {input threads × live threads × verdict} (AC2–AC5); coverage-counter test for reply targeting (AC2).
- `IT-*` — hermetic end-to-end of the rework pipeline with mocked SCM: drift fixture (threads appear mid-run) → completion lists them (AC5).
- `REG` — full `run_all.json` green; existing rework post-action tests stay green on the clean path (AC4).

## Non-goals

- Combining the CI-rework and threads-rework ARMERS into one rule (the armers stay separate; this card makes the LEG complete regardless of armer).
- #798 (silent-update vs in-flight leg race) — separate card, already filed.
- Changing the reply file format beyond requiring non-null threadId when threads exist (consumers elsewhere read this shape).

## Open questions

- Should `review_state.md` carry the reviewer's per-thread severity (BLOCKING/SUGGESTION) so the agent can prioritize? (GraphQL exposes it; recommend yes — cheap and useful.)

## References

- Live incident: run 37806292238 (untargeted reply, "no code changes required" while review required changes); follow-up review 18:37–18:56 (4 threads) → threads-armer → second rework leg 18:58 (4/4 resolved, run 37828431528).
- `preCliReworkSetup.js` steps 4.7/5–6; `githubHelpers.fetchDiscussionsAndRawData`; `gitOps.writePRContext`; `pushReworkChanges.js` completion-comment branch.
- Companion card: #798 (silent-update in-flight exclusion + push self-heal).

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

# gh-799: [ENH] Rework context preparation: guaranteed-complete rework picture (threads+CI+verdict) and honest live-rechecked completion — live: fa PR #1420

## Description

## Goal — Rework context preparation: guaranteed-complete rework picture + honest completion contract (v1)

One sentence: **every rework leg starts with the COMPLETE open-item picture of its PR (threads with IDs, CI failures, review verdict — regardless of which armer fired) and ends with a completion step that re-checks the PR live and never declares "no code changes required" while unresolved threads exist.**

Live evidence (fa PR #1420 / gh-1415, 2026-10-08): the CI-red-armed rework leg (run 37806292238) finished with `outputs/review_replies.json` carrying `"threadId": null` (untargeted reply → combined PR comment), and the post-action posted **"Rework Analysis Completed — AI Teammate analyzed all PR review comments and determined no code changes are required"** — while the PR's review state required changes. The threads themselves arrived later (18:56, posted by the follow-up review), so the input was honest at leg start — but the completion claim was written from the STALE input snapshot, not from the live PR, and nothing in the contract forces the agent to bind replies to thread IDs when threads exist. The machine loop self-corrected (threads-armer → second rework leg → 4/4 threads resolved), at the cost of an extra full leg + tokens and a misleading completion comment on the ticket.

## Why this framing

- `preCliReworkSetup.js` already fetches both halves of the picture (`ci_failures.md` step 4.7 + `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` → `pr_discussions.md` / `pr_discussions_raw.json` with IDs, step 5) — this card does not rebuild the pipeline; it closes three CONTRACT gaps around it: reply targeting, mid-run drift, and completion honesty.
- The silent-update race that also surfaced in the same leg is a separate card (#798) — out of scope here.

## Architecture

Three contract hardenings, all inside the existing rework pipeline (`preCliReworkSetup.js` input prep → `run-agent.sh` leg → `pushReworkChanges.js` post-action):

1. **Input completeness is armer-independent (pin it).** Whatever arms the leg (fail-validation CI-red, review-threads-resolved armer, conflict-rework, manual dispatch), the input folder must always carry: `pr_discussions_raw.json` (unresolved threads with IDs), `ci_failures.md` (failed checks), and a new `review_state.md` — the review verdict(s) + decision state (`CHANGES_REQUESTED` / `APPROVED` / none) — so the agent sees WHAT the reviewer asked, not just raw threads. Today the first two happen to be fetched; this card makes the trio a pinned contract with a test each (an armer that skips one is a regression).
2. **Reply-targeting contract.** `review_replies.json` rows must carry a non-null `threadId` whenever `pr_discussions_raw.json` held ≥1 unresolved thread at leg start; the post-action must treat "N threads in, fewer than N targeted replies out" as a LOUD warning state (per-thread coverage list in the log + completion comment), never silently fold untargeted replies into a "nothing required" story.
3. **Completion honesty (live re-check).** Before writing the completion ticket comment, the post-action re-fetches the PR's unresolved threads live (same call as input prep). Any thread that (a) appeared mid-run, or (b) was never targeted by a reply, is listed in the completion comment; the "no code changes are required" wording is allowed ONLY when the live unresolved-thread count is 0 AND the verdict is not CHANGES_REQUESTED. Everything else gets the truthful form: "rework pushed; N review threads remain open — the SM will re-arm a threads-rework."

## Capability surface

| step | today | after |
|---|---|---|
| input folder | threads + CI failures fetched (happens today, unpinned) | pinned trio + `review_state.md` verdict context, contract-tested |
| `review_replies.json` | threadId may be null even when threads exist | per-thread targeting required; coverage gap = loud warning |
| completion comment | template may claim "no code changes required" regardless of live state | live unresolved-thread re-check; honest wording, thread-by-thread accounting |
| machine loop | extra self-correction leg + misleading comment | one pass closes CI + threads; completion states exactly what remains |

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — a rework leg armed by ANY armer produces an input folder containing non-empty `pr_discussions_raw.json`, `ci_failures.md`, and `review_state.md` (fixture-tested per armer path).
